messages.content: What parameters do the viscous friction force depend on, and in which case should it be taken into account for the physical pendulum model? In your response the last word of each sentence must become the first word of the next sentence.

message.content: The viscous friction force depends on the velocity of the object and the viscosity coefficient of the surrounding medium. Medium characteristics like density and viscosity directly influence the damping force experienced by the pendulum. Pendulum models incorporating viscous friction should be used when the body oscillates within a fluid or when damping noticeably reduces the amplitude over time. Time-dependent decay of oscillations is the primary observable that signals the need to include the viscous term. Term inclusion is especially critical when high precision is required or when the pendulum swings through a liquid rather than a gas. Gas resistance is typically small for a simple pendulum in air, but it becomes significant at higher velocities or larger amplitudes. Amplitudes that produce substantial drag forces make the linear approximation inadequate, requiring a more complete model. Model accuracy is thus improved by accounting for the velocity-dependent resistive forces present in the environment.
